question: True or false: in 1841, when life expectancy in England and Wales was about 40, most adults died around 40.
answer: False. The average was dragged down by deaths in childhood. A five-year-old in 1841 could expect to reach about 55, and a 50-year-old about 71. Life expectancy at birth is a mean over everyone, and many died as babies, so it says little about when adults died.
move: An average over everyone can describe almost no one in particular.
ask: Which average have I read as the typical case when a few extremes shaped it?
trap: Reading life expectancy at birth as the usual age of death.
source: Our World in Data, life expectancy improved at all ages
